record.original_question: Must every rational map that has a Herman ring also have buried Julia components, or are additional global dynamical or topological assumptions needed before the existence of a Herman ring forces buried Julia components to appear?

evidence.quote: The presence of a Herman ring strongly suggests, but does not automatically guarantee, the existence of buried Julia components. In many known constructions, rational maps with Herman rings do exhibit buried Julia components arising from this topological separation. However, the existence of buried Julia components depends on the global arrangement of Fatou components and how the Julia set accumulates on their boundaries. It remains a subtle problem to determine whether every rational map with a Herman ring must contain buried Julia components or whether additional dynamical or topological conditions are required. As such, the question of whether Herman rings ensure the presence of buried Julia components is an important and largely open direction of investigation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ be a rational map of degree at least $2$ on the Riemann sphere. Recall:

- The Fatou set $F(f)$ is the set of points where the iterates $\{f^n\}$ form a normal family, and the Julia set is $J(f)=\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\setminus F(f)$.
- A Herman ring of $f$ is a periodic Fatou component $U$ (of period $p\geq 1$) on which $f^p:U\to U$ is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation $z\mapsto e^{2\pi i\alpha}z$ of a round annulus $\{1<|z|<r\}$.
- A connected component $K$ of $J(f)$ is called a buried Julia component if $K$ does not meet the boundary of any Fatou component of $f$; equivalently, $K\cap\partial U=\emptyset$ for every connected component $U$ of $F(f)$.

Question: Does every rational map $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ that admits a Herman ring necessarily have at least one buried Julia component? If not, determine additional global dynamical or topological hypotheses on $f$ under which the existence of a Herman ring forces the existence of a buried Julia component.
artifact.category_tag: Complex dynamics: Herman rings and Julia sets
artifact.status_search_result: Web sources show explicit constructions of rational maps with Herman rings that have buried Julia components (Godillon) and recent work on degenerate Herman rings, but none establishes a general implication or a counterexample. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A family of rational maps with buried Julia components (Godillon)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs rational maps possessing Herman rings whose Julia sets contain buried components of various topological types.
status_evidence.claim: Specific constructions exhibit Herman-ring maps with buried Julia components, but generality is not established.

status_evidence.title: Rational maps with smooth degenerate Herman rings
status_evidence.snippet: Studies degenerations of Herman rings and structure of associated Julia sets.
status_evidence.claim: Related structural questions are studied; the general implication is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Herman Rings: Structure, Dynamics, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the question of whether Herman rings force buried Julia components as a largely open direction.
status_evidence.claim: Survey treats this implication as open.
